courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Arts at Illinois
courses.description: Common Arts experience for FAA first-year students that explores contemporary issues in the arts, cross-disciplinary ingenuity navigating a comprehensive research intensive university, professional practices and exposures to FAA faculty and guest artists through lectures, discussion groups, and online components.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Design Beyond Boundaries
courses.description: This class surveys core issues and methods across a host of design disciplines, including industrial design, graphic design, interaction design, exhibition design, theatrical design, choreography, landscape architecture, and architecture. It explores the mindsets and methods with which designers develop innovative, user-oriented solutions to complex and persistent problems. Working individually and in diverse teams, students will deploy design process and design thinking to identify existing needs, frame and reframe problems, and ideate, iterate, and test original design solutions that defy conventional categories.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Exploring Arts and Creativity
courses.description: High and street art, tradition and experimentation, the familiar and unfamiliar, international and American creativity provide this course's foundation. Students will attend performances and exhibitions, interact with artists, and examine core issues associated with the creative process in our increasingly complex global society. Faculty from the arts, sciences, humanities, and other domains will lead students through visual arts, music, dance, and theatre experiences at Krannert Center and Krannert Art Museum to spark investigation and dialogue.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Elements of Hip Hop
courses.description: Explores the origins and evolutions of Hip Hop culture through the elements of DJing, Emceeing, Breaking, Graffiti, and Knowledge. The course features asynchronous video lectures from university faculty, assigned readings and multimedia content, interactive online discussions, and assessments designed to synthesize and apply course material.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Undergraduate Open Seminar
courses.description: Various special topics in Fine and Applied Arts. See class schedule for offerings. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated in the same or separate semesters to a maximum of 6 hours if topics vary; some restrictions may apply.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Black Arts Today
courses.description: A global course in theorizing Black cultural expression. It surveys artistic and cultural responses to types of racism (racial formations), modes of Black resistance and resiliency, and expressions of Black liberation and self-determination. Topics range from Spirituals, Gospel, and "ring-shouts" to Western classical music, ballet and modern dance; from Blues, Jazz, and Hip-Hop to African-inspired architecture and Blues tropes embedded in urban and regional segregationist planning; and from the lineage of Black Art + Design to the power of place of the Black Metropolis. As such, the course attends to the geographies of place and ontologies of time, i.e., moments formed from the intersection of Black social movements against white supremacy and Black reimagining of what it means to be human. Through a series of engagements with faculty-artists and researchers in the College of Fine & Applied Arts, Black Arts Today explores the practice and speculative spaces (imaginaries) in which FAA artists-instructors-researchers engage Black Arts or transmit Blackness to the arts.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Artsful Teaching through Integ
courses.description: Designed to provide elementary education majors with a philosophical and practical basis for integrating the arts [including visual art, music, & dance] in public schools. Lecture, discussion, arts practices and class activities will focus on the ever expanding role of the arts in children's lives and the role of the teacher in nurturing artistic expressions through the development of skills, processes, and the various knowledges of the multi-modalities of the arts. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to students who have completed applicable Teacher Licensure Gateway requirements. Contact College of Education for further information. Admission to the Elementary Teacher Education Program.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Sustainable Design of the Built Environment
courses.description: This seminar introduces fundamental readings in sustainability and resilient design. Presents diverse perspectives on sustainability, encouraging students to understand and critique different meanings of sustainability over time and geography. Approved for Letter and S/U grading.
courses.prereqText: Priority given for majors.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Tools for Sustainable Design Studio
courses.description: Introduces students to the principles, tools, and practices at the core of contemporary sustainable design. The course emphasizes material ecology, circularity, and life cycle analysis, inviting students to understand design as a system of interdependent environmental, social, and material factors.
courses.prereqText: ARCH 171. For Sustainable Design majors only. Sophomore standing required.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Disability in the Arts
courses.description: Critically examines issues of access, embodiment, and representation in art, design, film, and the performing arts. Whereas cultural producers and institutions shape our understanding of disability, this course will explore/interrogate how disability is constructed, communicated, and represented in the arts. Through creative projects, artistic research, and a series of regular viewing/reading discussions, students will develop a personalized critical and aesthetic vernacular through which to engage contemporary Disability/Crip discourses.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Creative Access: Crip/Disabled Strategies for Belonging
courses.description: Introduction to and experimentation with creative accessibility strategies. Contemporary discourse surrounding Crip Theory and Critical Disability Studies addresses a need to incorporate inclusive and intersectional accessibility principles into the framework of cultural production and public engagement. This course will emphasize locating and transforming access/accessibility in our daily lives and community connections, guided by the concept of ‘access ecology’ where access is something we create collectively and that responds to each of our individual needs.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Disability in/around Film
courses.description: Explores Crip/Disabled culture, concepts, and histories through the lens of film and video. Each week students will experience different Crip/Disabled films and explore some of the concepts, challenges, and critiques that surround and support them. Through an exploration of Crip/Disabled knowledge, history(s), principles, and methods in/around film and video, students will develop a personalized critical and aesthetic vernacular through which to engage contemporary Disability/Crip discourses.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Figures and Figurations of Crip/Disabled Arts and Culture
courses.description: Access/accessibility is something we make together that responds to the needs and desires of each of our bodyminds. This course will critically engage issues of access, embodiment, and representation in the arts through a survey of pivotal figures that shape Crip/Disability culture. Through this we will develop an understanding of how disability is constructed, communicated, and represented in the arts. This course will emphasize locating and transforming access/accessibility in our daily lives applying the body of knowledge developed by each figure/figuration surveyed.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Crip Cinema—Disability in/around Film, Video and Experimental Media
courses.description: Examines how time-based media alters how objects, bodies, and landscapes are activated, supported, imagined, and treated. Students will engage in the applied research strategies and creative methodologies of Crip Cinema in order to develop a deeper understanding of access, embodiment, and representational issues. Through the course students will explore and enact cripistemological writing/text/descriptive methods that are guided by the Crip* principles of interdependence, open access, Crip Time, networks of support and collaboration, and access ecology.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Design Lab I
courses.description: A project-based course where students from diverse fields collaborate on creative design challenges. Working in teams, they will conceptualize, prototype, and showcase interactive experiences informed by human-centered design. Emphasizing storytelling, structured feedback, and critical reflection, the course develops collaborative and creative problem-solving skills. Each semester introduces a new design challenge, preparing students for work in game design, interactive media, and related creative industries. May be repeated in separate terms up to 12 UG hours.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: FAA Study Abroad
courses.description: Provides campus credit for foreign study and/or travel. A detailed proposal for study abroad must be submitted for approval by the appropriate committee of the department in which the student is studying and the college dean's office prior to such study abroad. Final determination of credit and its application toward the degree is made after a review of the student's work abroad by the above committee and college office. (summer session, 0 to 6 undergraduate hours). Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated to a maximum of 36 hours.
courses.prereqText: Approval of the student's proposal by the departmental committee and the college office.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Arts at Illinois
courses.description: Introduces students to interdisciplinary arts while providing an advanced orientation to online learning. Students will explore and refine their personal and professional interests, design an intentional educational pathway, and strengthen skills in time management, goal setting, and professional communication. Emphasis is placed on cultivating ethical and culturally informed perspectives, connecting prior experiences to academic growth, and preparing for future career aspirations in the arts and beyond.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to online BA in FAA majors.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: FAA Professional Development
courses.description: Focuses on tailoring written, verbal, and online presentations to targeted audiences. Students will develop an application package including resume, letter, LinkedIn profile, elevator pitch, interview skills, and website.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to sophomores, juniors, or seniors in FAA.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Off-Campus Internship in Arts, Design, and Creative Industries
courses.description: Opportunity to apply principles and practices of the applied fine and applied arts through meaningful, supervised work experiences in professional creative settings. Students engage in hands-on projects that integrate artistic theory, technical skills, and creative problem-solving within real-world contexts, benefiting both the host organization and the student’s professional development. Emphasis is placed on connecting classroom learning to practical application, fostering professional growth, and preparing students for careers in the applied and fine arts. Students must submit an approved internship to faa-uaa@illinois.edu to request registration in this course. Internships are not provided to students, you must apply and receive an offer independently and email the job description and offer letter to be considered for enrollment in this academic course with credit. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in separate terms up to 6 undergraduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to students with Sophomore standing and good academic standing.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Field Trip / Experiential Learning in the Arts
courses.description: Provides an interdisciplinary field-based exploration of fine and applied arts through direct engagement with artistic and creative environments. Students participate in guided visits examining practices across visual, performing, and applied arts disciplines. Emphasis is placed on observational analysis, contextual understanding, and the integration of multiple artistic perspectives. Through reflection, discussion, and documentation, students connect experiential learning to broader cultural, historical, and theoretical frameworks, fostering critical inquiry, creative thinking, and professional engagement in diverse arts contexts. Approved for both Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Faculty-Led Global Learning Abroad
courses.description: Short-term, faculty-led study abroad course led by FAA faculty or staff combining academic instruction with immersive, field-based learning in an international setting. Includes pre-departure preparation, on-site engagement, and reflective assignments focused on global and cultural understanding. Approved for both Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Making Sustainable Design
courses.description: Introduction to techniques and tools for representing and realizing sustainable design ideas. Using a case study method, students are introduced to digital and analog means of representing concepts, data, and spatial forms. Through hands-on assignments, tutorials, and workshops, students learn basic skills to express ideas graphically and in three dimensions.
courses.prereqText: ARCH 171 and a drawing course. Restricted to Sustainable Design major.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Sustainable Design Internship
courses.description: Supervised field experience in a full-time or part-time internship position related to the field of Sustainable Design. Designed to introduce students to professional employment and actual practice. Full documentation and approval of internship activities required. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of three times.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to Sustainable Design majors only. Registration only with instructor permission (sustaindesign@illinois.edu).

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Various special topics in Fine and Applied Arts. See class schedule for offerings. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated in the same or separate semesters to a maximum of 6 hours if topics vary; with permission of the unit advisor.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Imagining Futures through the Arts
courses.description: In this course, students synthesize their coursework and experiences. Students will examine industries and projects of interest and envision their aspirations. It is the culminating course in the BA in FAA degree program. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.
courses.prereqText: FAA 310. Restricted to online BA in FAA majors.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Experience Design for Immersion & Interaction
courses.description: Explores participant-centered experience design in immersive and interactive formats, including theatre, games, and other experiences. Students will examine participant journeys, build experience frameworks, and iterate on prototypes, culminating in a fully designed immersive and/or interactive experience.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Sustainable Design Capstone Seminar
courses.description: Introduces advanced research themes, methods, and techniques for seniors in the Bachelor of Science in Sustainable Design. Emphasis is placed on students developing their own research topics, using multiple representational forms, including writing, drawing, mapping, and modeling. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.
courses.prereqText: FAA 230 and FAA 330. Restricted to majors only. Senior standing required.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Sustainable Design Capstone Studio
courses.description: In design studio format, students work on capstone projects for the Bachelor of Science in Sustainable Design degree. Students receive regular feedback and critique throughout the semester in the form of desk critiques, pin-ups, and formal reviews with Illinois Faculty and guests from other institutions. 5 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.
courses.prereqText: FAA 430. Restricted to undergraduate majors.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Design Lab II
courses.description: Expanding on foundational skills, students explore advanced creative territories with independence and conceptual depth. Interdisciplinary teams design innovative, playable experiences that push boundaries while remaining responsive to human needs and contexts. Through collaboration, prototyping, and iteration, students cultivate unique creative voices and produce portfolio-quality work. Emphasizing creative risk-taking and conceptual development, the course supports emerging identities as designers while fostering artistic vision grounded in thoughtful, human-centered design. 1 TO 3 undergraduate hours. 1 TO 3 graduate hours. May be repeated in separate terms up to 12 undergraduate hours or up to 12 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: FAA 250 (undergraduates only).

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Advanced Studies in Hip Hop
courses.description: Explores Hip Hop topics within cultural, social, geographic, historical, and political contexts in order to inform the generation of original artistic work and scholarship. Students are expected to have some experience with visual and/or performing arts as well as scholarly reading and writing. Intended for upper-level undergraduates and graduate students. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 9 undergraduate or 12 graduate hours.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Hip Hop Ambassadors
courses.description: Explores Hip Hop youth programming through engagement with relevant literature and the design and delivery of programs in school and community settings. Students will attend a weekly seminar as well as spend 1-3 hours per week participating in field experience in the local community. Most field experience assignments will be within existing programs, and students will have opportunities to develop new smaller scale events as well. 3 or 4 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 11 undergraduate or 12 graduate hours. All students will need to complete Protection of Minors training and a criminal background check in order to work with minors during the semester. Some field experience locations may have additional requirements for participation. Contact the course instructor for further details about days, times, locations, and requirements of current field experience programs.
courses.prereqText: Instructor permission required to enroll.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Minoritarian Aesthetics Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study of a theoretical or creative project on a topic in the field of minoritarian aesthetics. Minoritarian Aesthetics is an interdisciplinary field focusing on performance and aesthetics as inseparable from social life. It values minoritarian practices and community involvement across the arts as a lens to examine the complex worlds we communally navigate and share. Students in this course engage in study beyond the current MA course offerings with attention paid to original research. 1 to 4 undergraduate hours. 1 to 4 graduate hours. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Instructor approval required.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Special Problems in Sustainable Design
courses.description: Directed independent creative activity or research. 1 to 4 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit. May be repeated to a maximum of 12 hours.
courses.prereqText: 3.3 GPA minimum required to enroll. A contract must be completed & approved. Consent of instructor and faculty administrator for Sustainable Design. Junior or Senior standing in Sustainable Design.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: MAL Practical Engagement Opportunity
courses.description: Students will broaden their understanding of the field of Minoritarian Aesthetics through practical engagement and shadowing working professionals. Under the advisement of the Minor Aesthetics Lab (MAL), students will seek experiences to enhance their educational experience and develop essential skills required within the field. A list of ideas will be provided, although students are ultimately responsible for finding and securing their shadow or practical engagement opportunity. Full documentation and approval of activities required. 1 undergraduate hour. No graduate credit. Approved for Letter and S/U grading.
courses.prereqText: For Minoritarian Aesthetics undergraduate minors who have completed at least 12 credit hours towards the minor.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Writing with Performance: Politics of Love
courses.description: How do we tell the truth about love? What does love have to do with performances on stage, in everyday life, and social and cultural politics? To critically consider the theoretical, performative, cultural, and social manifestations of love, we will turn to texts moving across theory, poetry, dramatic literature to aesthetic sites like live performance, performance art, music, and visual culture to analyze diverse ways of seeking and giving affection. Same as AAS 494, ENGL 494, GWS 494, and THEA 484. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Minoritarian Aesthetics Practicum
courses.description: Following a minoritarian aesthetics compass, informed by the disciplines of relational ethnic and performance studies, students will approach critical theory, embodied practice, and collective learning as inseparable. Working closely with one another and with guest artists, scholars, teachers, and curators, as well as practice-based initiatives such as the Mellon funded Minor Aesthetics Lab, students will be asked to display and/or perform their work within the tradition of fusing aesthetics and social life. Same as AAS 495, ENGL 495, GWS 425, and THEA 468. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Experiments in Queer of Color Performance
courses.description: Engages queer performance across sound, image, text, and embodiment. Students will read and experiment across texts in performance studies, feminist, trans, and queer studies, visual culture, cultural studies, sound studies, and relational ethnic studies. By moving through the entanglement of performance, politics, and difference, students will pay attention to forms of resistance, revolt, survival, everyday endurance strategies, and diverse types of cultural labor witnessed across queerness. Same as AAS 496, ENGL 496, GWS 496, and THEA 486. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Crip* Research Internship
courses.description: Supervised experience designed for creative and interdisciplinary research projects led by faculty in the College of Fine and Applied Arts. 0 to 4 undergraduate hours. 0 to 4 graduate hours. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of six (6) hours.
courses.prereqText: Instructor permission required.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Crip* Advanced Study
courses.description: Undergraduate examination of Cripistemology and the Arts through independent study and/or group seminars. Crip* is a practice-based, experimental creative research project and transdisciplinary initiative that critically engages notions of access, embodiment, and representation and aims to develop a creative methodology founded in the application of critical epistemologies. Students in this advanced study course are supported in developing in-depth Crip*-informed research praxes in/around Crip/Disabled arts + culture, cripistemology, and other Crip* principles. 1 TO 4 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated for a maximum of 8 credit hours.
courses.prereqText: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics in subject areas within the College of Fine and Applied Arts intended to augment the existing curriculum. 0 to 4 undergraduate hours. 0 to 4 graduate hours. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated in separate terms if topics vary to a maximum of 8 credit hours.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: deaf*- In/Around Art + Communication
courses.description: Graduate examination of deaf*—a term to describe a multiplicity of non-normative experiences, vantages, and epistemologies in/around aurality, orality, communication, listening, and beyond— is emergent, speculative, re: generative, and horizontal (of/towards the sensorium’s horizon). This course will explore, chart, apply, and expand upon deaf* creative/critical methodologies through a combination of theoretical, practical, and historical modes. May be repeated.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Crip* Temporalities—Crip/Disabled Embodiment and Time-Based Praxes
courses.description: Performance, film/video, theatre, dance, sound, and other temporally engaged cultural and political modes alter how objects, bodies, and landscapes are activated, supported, imagined, and treated. This course will explore time-based creative/critical methodologies through the embodied frameworks of disability, Crip Theory, and cripistemology. Students will develop bespoke crip* temporalities that respond to dominant discourses of disability and the intersection of performance studies and disability studies. May be repeated.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Cripistemological Archive(s)—Preserving Crip/Disabled Histories
courses.description: Explores the preservation, documentation, and generation of Crip/Disabled histories by applying a cripistemological framework to creative and critical archive research and praxes. This course will serve as an introduction to and an implementation of creative accessibility strategies pertinent to the surfacing, collecting, documenting, archiving, and disseminating of Crip/Disabled knowledge(s). Guided by Crip* principles such as interdependence, open access, networks of support and collaboration, Crip temporalities, and access ecology, students will develop a cripistemological working method. May be repeated.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Cripistemology and the Arts Seminar
courses.description: Crip*- Cripistemology and the Arts (Crip*) is a practice based creative research project and transdisciplinary initiative focused on how knowledge produced via Crip/Disabled experience can shape and change how we approach our respective mediums. Courses will explore specializations within the Crip* discipline and include attending lectures, screenings, workshops and performances outside of class time. Subjects include Crip* Temporalities: Crip/Disabled Embodiment and Time-Based Praxes, deaf*: Art and Communication, and Crip* Collaboration: Experiments in Crip/Disabled Cultural Formations. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 12 graduate hours.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Cripping FAA
courses.description: Critically and creatively engages the applied research strategies, creative methodologies, and disciplinary conventions via the Crip* principles of interdependence, open access, generative difference, radical alterity, networks of support and collaboration, Crip temporalities, and access ecology. This course will serve to discover and design new crip-centric approaches and strategies to interdisciplinary fields in the College of Fine and Applied Arts.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Cripping Art + Design
courses.description: Cripping Art & Design critically and creatively engages the applied research strategies, creative methodologies, and disciplinary conventions of Art and Design fields via the Crip* principles of interdependence, open access, generative difference, radical alterity, networks of support and collaboration, Crip temporalities, and access ecology. This course will serve to discover and design new crip-centric approaches and strategies specific to Art and Design disciplines. Same as ART 553. Approved for Letter and S/U grading.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Cripping Dance
courses.description: Critically and creatively engages the applied research strategies, creative methodologies, and disciplinary conventions of Dance via the Crip* principles of interdependence, open access, generative difference, radical alterity, networks of support and collaboration, Crip temporalities, and access ecology. This course will serve to discover and design new crip-centric approaches and strategies specific to Dance. Same as DANC 554.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Cripping Landscape Architecture
courses.description: Critically and creatively engages the applied research strategies, creative methodologies, and disciplinary conventions of Landscape Architecture via the Crip* principles of interdependence, open access, generative difference, radical alterity, networks of support and collaboration, Crip temporalities, and access ecology. This course will serve to discover and design new crip-centric approaches and strategies specific to Landscape Architecture. Same as LA 555.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Cripping Music
courses.description: Cripping Music critically and creatively engages the applied research strategies, creative methodologies, and disciplinary conventions of Music via the Crip* principles of interdependence, open access, generative difference, radical alterity, networks of support and collaboration, Crip temporalities, and access ecology. This course will serve to discover and design new crip-centric approaches and strategies specific to Music. Same as MUS 566. Approved for Letter and S/U grading.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Cripping Theatre
courses.description: Critically and creatively engages the applied research strategies, creative methodologies, and disciplinary conventions of Theatre via the Crip* principles of interdependence, open access, generative difference, radical alterity, networks of support and collaboration, Crip temporalities, and access ecology. This course will serve to discover and design new crip-centric approaches and strategies specific to Theatre. Same as THEA 557.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Cripping Urban Planning
courses.description: Critically and creatively engages the applied research strategies, creative methodologies, and disciplinary conventions of Urban & Regional Planning via the Crip* principles of interdependence, open access, generative difference, radical alterity, networks of support and collaboration, Crip temporalities, and access ecology. This course will serve to discover and design new crip-centric approaches and strategies specific to Urban & Regional Planning. Same as UP 558.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Writing the Minor - Minoritarian Aesthetics
courses.description: This seminar focuses on interdisciplinary research across critical writing within the field of minoritarian aesthetics. Drawing from performance studies and ethnic studies, students will move across everyday social and cultural world making practices to write with and for difference. Class sessions will include live readings, writing exercises, writing workshops, and discussions with published authors in the field. This is an intensive writing course; students will write during class session to produce a pressing publishable paper. Same as AAS 594, ENGL 594, GWS 594, and THEA 594.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Experiments in Minoritarian Aesthetics
courses.description: Engaging aesthetics beyond its common understanding as the branch of philosophy concerned with the appreciation of art and culture, this course follows the vitality of the aesthetic through pathways into the pressing cultural expressions of minoritarian life. Students will be asked to take on new learning gestures, to think of study as a minoritarian aesthetic practice, and to think of study writ large as an act of new world-making. Same as AAS 596, ENGL 596, GWS 596, and THEA 596.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Crip* Graduate Directed Research
courses.description: Directed research project or creative project in the area of Cripistemology and the Arts. Approved for both Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated.
courses.prereqText: Instructor approval required. Restricted to graduate students in good standing.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Graduate Special Topics
courses.description: Advanced special topics in graduate subject areas within the College of Fine and Applied Arts intended to augment the existing curriculum. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated for a maximum of 8 credit hours.

courses.subject: FAA
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: Individual direction of research and thesis writing. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in separate terms up to 32 G hours.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Fine and Applied Arts.
